scope.full_target:
A sphere-valued map cannot vanish outside a compact set. As approved by
the user on 2026-10-23, interpret spatial compact support as compact support
of a perturbation from a **fixed unit vector**, locally uniformly in time.
This is a disclosed nontrivial interpretation, not a claimed author-issued
correction.

Let \(n,m\geq1\) be integers and let
\(u:\mathbb R^n\times(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R^m\) be jointly smooth.
Fix \(q\in\mathbb R^m\) with \(|q|=1\). Assume:

1. \(|u(x,t)|=1\) for all \(x\) and \(t>0\).
2. The acceleration \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu\) is normal to the sphere at
   \(u\): at each point there is a real scalar \(a(x,t)\) with
   \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu=a u\). No regularity of the selected scalar is
   assumed.
3. For every \(0<s<t<\infty\), a compact set
   \(C_{[s,t]}\subset\mathbb R^n\) exists such that \(u(x,r)=q\) for
   \(x\notin C_{[s,t]}\), \(r\in[s,t]\).

With Euclidean norms and Lebesgue measure, define

\[
e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|^2+\sum_{j=1}^n|\partial_{x_j}u(x,t)|^2,
\qquad E(t)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e(x,t)\,dx.
\]

The spatial gradient square is the Frobenius square, and
\(\Delta_xu=\sum_j\partial_{x_jx_j}u\) component by component.
Prove integrability of \(e(\cdot,t)\), differentiability of \(E\),
and \(E'(t)=0\) for every \(t>0\). No assertion at time zero is required.

hypotheses.statement: u is jointly C∞ on ℝⁿ×(0,∞).
q∈ℝᵐ satisfies |q|=1 for the Euclidean norm.
For every x∈ℝⁿ and t>0, |u(x,t)|=1 for the Euclidean norm.
For every x∈ℝⁿ and t>0 there exists a real scalar a such that u_tt(x,t)−Δ_x u(x,t)=a u(x,t), with Δ_x u=∑_{j=1}^n ∂_{x_jx_j}u componentwise. No regularity or global choice of the scalar is assumed.

binders.type: compact subset of ℝⁿ, existentially bound

hypotheses.statement: For every pair of real numbers 0<s<t<∞ there exists a compact C⊆ℝⁿ such that u(x,r)=q for every x∉C and every r∈[s,t].

source.statement: For every real t>0, e(·,t) is Lebesgue integrable on ℝⁿ, the finite energy E is differentiable at t, and E'(t)=0. Here e=|u_t|²+∑_{j=1}^n|∂_{x_j}u|² and E(t)=∫_{ℝⁿ}e(x,t) dx with Euclidean norms and Lebesgue measure; there is no assertion at time zero.

correspondence.explanation: Parameters n,m are natural dimensions with H001 enforcing n,m≥1, equivalent to the specified positive integer dimensions. The parameter u has exactly the original positive-time domain in fixed standard coordinates; q is the fixed vector. H002 requires smoothness only on the positive open half-space of its canonical extension ubar, equivalent in both directions to joint smoothness of the original map by restriction and local agreement. H003 and H004 use normSq=∑k v_k²=1, equivalent over ℝ to Euclidean norm 1 since that norm is nonnegative. H005 retains ∀x,t>0 ∃a:ℝ with A−L=a•ubar and imposes no regularity or global choice of a. H006 keeps ∀0<s<t ∃compact C ∀x∉C ∀r∈[s,t], ubar=q, so support remains locally uniform in time. Restricting ubar recovers u and extending u by q recovers ubar; all derivatives at positive times are local and unchanged. Standard coordinate identities preserve the finite-dimensional topology and Fréchet derivatives in both directions, while normSq and finite spatial sums are exactly the Euclidean and Frobenius squares and volume is exactly product Lebesgue measure. The conclusion explicitly quantifies every real t>0 and proves integrability of the coefficient-1 density, DifferentiableAt of its actual energy integral, and deriv=0. Thus the complete target and all hypotheses correspond in both directions; there is no additional assertion at zero, stronger support requirement, or assumption on the scalar witness.
